newsitem.title: UK: SOCCER-FOWLER WILL STAY AT LIVERPOOL.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-FOWLER WILL STAY AT LIVERPOOL.

text.p: Striker Robbie Fowler has pledged his long-term future to English premier league club Liverpool and has no desire to try his luck on the continent.
Fowler, 21, says it is the influx of foreign stars that makes him want to stay in England.
"I've never thought about going anywhere else, I'm very happy at Liverpool," he said.
"Top players are coming over here now so it shows that we are going in the right direction and what a good league it will turn out to be.
"I don't see any reason why I should want to leave to play in another league as the premier league is going to be one of the best in the world.

"The atmosphere in the grounds is first class, you play against good teams and players. The likes of the Vialli's - how many European trophies as he won? - to play against these guys is incentive enough to stay here in itself."
Fowler also warned the rest of the league that Liverpool are back to their best.

"After a shaky patch it's getting on the right track again. And with the squad we've got it should be _ just look at the players we had on the bench in the League Cup tie against Arsenal: Collymore, Redknapp and Matteo.
"That says it all. Hopefully we'll start winning major trophies and no-one will want to leave." Liverpool won the match 4-2 on Wednesday.
Fowler has been named in the 50 players short-listed for the European Player of the Year award and is delighted by the recognition.
"Even though I don't think I'll win it, it's still nice to be there," he said.
"I only made two appearances as sub for England in Euro 96. It's nice to be recognised all around Europe for what I do for Liverpool."
